sections.title: The letter ü
paragraphs: The letter (Ü) /yː/ is named (Ü) /yː/. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. It mainly makes the vowel sound heard in (Übung) /ˈyːbʊŋ/, which means exercise, practice. This letter has two different sounds.

sections.title: Making the sounds
paragraphs: For the first sound, lift your tongue high and forward like the vowel in see. At the same time, push your lips forward into a small tight circle. Keep your voice on and hold the sound. For the second sound, relax your tongue slightly down and keep your lips in a loose circle. Check your throat with your hand to feel the vibration.

sections.title: Reading the variants
paragraphs: A syllable is one beat of a word. When this letter stands in an open or stressed syllable, it is long. You hear this sound in (Tür) /tyːɐ̯/. A consonant cluster is two or more consonants side by side. Before double consonants or consonant clusters, the sound is short. You hear this shorter variant in (fünf) /fʏnf/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not replace this vowel with the English sound in moon or boot. Pulling your tongue back to make the vowel in boot changes the word completely. Instead, say the vowel in see and push your lips forward into a tight ring. Do not let your lips spread flat like the vowel in pit. Keep your lips pushed forward throughout the entire sound.
